answers.value: Every in-scope submission/renewal account bound or quoted in the quarter for the underwriter's book (commercial property & casualty), reviewed for coverage gaps, sublimit adequacy and deductible appropriateness against the account's exposure schedule and the filed appetite.
The current quarter's new-business and renewal effective dates (e.g. 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30); accounts with effective dates outside the quarter are excluded from this review cycle.

Each account record shows: total insured value, per-peril sublimits, deductibles/retentions, coverage forms attached, and the exposure schedule (COPE/SIC/class). Records missing an exposure schedule or with a null TIV are returned to the submission intake queue as incomplete.

Account count in the coverage-gap worklist reconciles to the bound/quoted count in Guidewire PolicyCenter for the quarter; delta must be 0. Any account in PolicyCenter absent from the worklist is logged as a coverage-review gap.

The gap-analysis memo (identified gaps, recommended sublimits/deductibles, disposition) is filed to the account folder in PolicyCenter and the underwriting workstation with version label and timestamp; retained 7 years per state file-documentation requirements.

Uninsurable or appetite-exceeding gaps are logged as an exception with disposition (referral, coverage decline, or documented waiver) and routed to a Senior Underwriter within 2 business days; disposition and rationale recorded on the account file.

Adequacy is assessed against the current underwriting-guideline and appetite version (Commercial UW Guide v6.1) and the schedule-rating worksheet; the guide version in force on the effective date governs the review.

Sublimit adequacy is flagged when a modeled loss scenario (e.g. 100-yr PML or largest foreseeable single loss) exceeds the applicable sublimit by more than 10%; deductible sensitivity tested at +/- one deductible band.

A coverage gap is treated as material and must be documented/referred where the uninsured exposure exceeds $250,000 or 5% of TIV, whichever is lower; immaterial gaps are noted but do not require referral.

Pre/post comparison: the account's coverage schedule before the review is diffed against the recommended schedule; the memo confirms every material gap either closed by endorsement or dispositioned; comparison attached to the account file.
Coverage or endorsement changes arising from the review are raised as a policy-change transaction in PolicyCenter and cross-referenced to the gap-analysis memo id on the account file.
A quarterly quality sample of 25 reviewed accounts (or 10% of the book, whichever is greater), stratified across property, casualty and package business.

PASS = documented gap-analysis memo present, all material gaps (>$250k or 5% TIV) dispositioned, sublimits/deductibles justified against appetite. FAIL = missing memo, an undocumented material gap, or a sublimit outside guideline with no referral.

Failed files are returned to the owning Underwriter for remediation within 5 business days; unresolved authority-exceeding gaps escalate to a Senior Underwriter, and systemic patterns feed the quarterly UW quality report.
Acceptance = 100% of sampled accounts carry a gap-analysis memo, zero undocumented material gaps, and every recommended sublimit/deductible traceable to the appetite/guideline in force.
Evidence (memos, exception log, QA sample results) is stored in the underwriting workstation under /uw-quality/coverage-adequacy/<quarter>/ and linked from the PolicyCenter account file.

checklist.step: Assess each account's coverage against the documented appetite by line of business, geography and industry
checklist.value: Recommended sublimits/deductibles are checked against the Commercial UW Guide appetite table for the account's LOB/class; out-of-appetite exposures flagged for referral.

testing.step: Verify appetite alignment on sampled files
testing.value: For the 25-file sample, 100% of coverage recommendations reconcile to the current appetite table; any deviation carries a documented authority approval.

checklist.step: Document the coverage-gap and adequacy findings on the account file
checklist.value: Gap-analysis memo filed in PolicyCenter with identified gaps, recommendations and disposition, versioned and dated.

testing.value: Sampled accounts show a complete gap-analysis memo; 0 files with material gaps and no supporting documentation.

testing.value: 100% of above-threshold accounts in the sample show a recorded Senior Underwriter review with sign-off date.

answers.value: The external data ordered for each account under review: prior-carrier loss runs (5-year), MVRs, credit-based insurance scores/consumer reports, LexisNexis/CLUE reports and property risk data, scoped to the submissions in the underwriter's current work queue.

Reports received reconcile to reports ordered for the account; ordered-vs-received delta must be 0 before the file moves to analysis. Outstanding orders past 3 business days are re-requested and logged.

Missing, stale or no-hit reports are logged as exceptions with disposition (re-order, alternate provider, or proceed with documented rationale); consumer-report data-quality disputes routed to the provider within 2 business days.
Ordering follows the current data-ordering standard operating procedure (Data Order SOP v4) specifying which reports are mandatory by line of business and premium band.
Loss-run adequacy is sensitive to the lookback window: fewer than 5 years or a gap in coverage years triggers a request for supplemental history before pricing proceeds.
A missing mandatory report on an account with premium above $100,000 is material and blocks quoting; below that threshold the underwriter may proceed with a documented data-limitation note.

Parameters (subject identifiers, coverage years, permissible-purpose codes) sourced from the submission record in PolicyCenter and the broker submission packet.

answers.value: The trailing five-year loss history for the risk under review: prior-carrier loss runs and internal claims history covering paid + outstanding (incurred) losses, claim counts, and large-loss detail for the account's coverages.
The five most recent complete policy years prior to the proposed effective date (e.g. 2021-2025 for a 2026 effective policy); partial or open policy years are noted as immature.

Summed loss-run totals reconcile to the year-by-year detail and to any internal claims extract for shared years; a variance over 2% is investigated and reconciled before the history is used in pricing.

Missing years, stale valuations (>90 days old) or unexplained development are logged as exceptions with disposition (re-request, actuarial referral, or documented adjustment) and resolved before firm quote.
Loss development and trend factors applied to the history follow the current pricing/loss-analysis methodology (Loss Analysis Guide v3); the version in force at quote date governs.

Burn-cost is sensitive to large losses: individual claims above the account's expected severity are shown gross and capped, and the effect of excluding/including them on the indicated rate is documented.
A loss-year restatement or newly reported large loss that moves indicated loss cost by more than 5% is material and triggers a re-review and, above authority, a Senior Underwriter/actuarial referral.

Any correction to loaded loss data is made via a policy-transaction/data-correction note in PolicyCenter, cross-referenced to the loss-run source document on the account file.
Quarterly sample of 25 accounts checked for a complete, reconciled five-year loss review supporting the pricing decision.
PASS = five complete loss years present, totals reconciled within 2%, large losses and development documented. FAIL = missing loss years, unreconciled totals, or an undocumented material large loss.
Failures return to the Underwriter to re-request or reconcile within 5 business days; material adverse development above authority escalates to a Senior Underwriter and, where indicated, actuarial.
Loss Analysis Guide v3 governs development/trend selection; the version in force at quote date is recorded on the file.
Loss amounts and valuation dates sourced from prior-carrier loss runs and the internal claims system extract; trend/development factors sourced from the actuarial loss-cost parameter set.

Field definitions (policy_period, paid, outstanding, incurred, claim_count, valuation_date) come from the loss-run data dictionary; control total = sum of annual incurred equals the loss-run grand total, reconciled within 2% and cross-checked to the internal claims extract for overlapping years.

Filings and correspondence closed in the current filing period plus the statutory retention tail; archived within 30 days of a filing reaching closed/approved status in SERFF.

Archived filing count reconciles to closed filings in SERFF for the period; delta must be 0. Any closed SERFF filing without an archived correspondence set is logged as an archival gap.

Correspondence and approvals are archived to the filed-forms records repository (Archer GRC record + SERFF) with immutable timestamp and version; retained per each state's record-retention rule (minimum 7 years / policy life + 5 where longer).

Incomplete or unmatched correspondence is logged as an exception with disposition (retrieve from SERFF, request from DOI, or document as unavailable) and cleared before the filing is marked archived; owner = Product Filing Specialist.

Retention and examination-access are driven by each state's insurance record-retention statute and market-conduct examination rules; the applicable citation is recorded on the archive index for each state.
Retention met: records held for the longer of 7 years or the state-mandated period; disposition holds are honored and destruction is suppressed while a market-conduct exam or litigation hold is open.
Archival completed within 30 days of filing closure; the archive index shows the closure date and archived date so the SLA is auditable.
A quarterly sample of 25 closed filings inspected for a complete, retrievable correspondence-and-approval archive.

PASS = every sampled filing has an indexed archive containing objections, responses and the approval notice, retrievable within the retention rule. FAIL = any missing approval notice, unindexed correspondence, or record not retrievable on request.
Gaps are remediated by the Product Filing Specialist within 10 business days; records unavailable from SERFF are requested from the DOI and the gap is tracked in Archer GRC until closed.
Field definitions (serff_tracking, state, lob, filing_type, disposition, approval_date, doc_links) come from the filing-archive index data dictionary.
Control total = closed filings in SERFF for the period equals archived filing records in the repository; reconciled to 0 variance each quarter.

Applicable rule = the relevant state insurance record-retention statute and NAIC Market Regulation Handbook examination-access expectations; the specific state citation is recorded on each archived filing's index entry.

Non-acknowledged recipients after 5 business days are re-notified and escalated to their manager; unresolved non-acknowledgement before effective date is logged as an exception with disposition.
The notice cites the SERFF tracking number and DOI approval date for the form change so recipients can trace the regulatory basis for the update.
The notification and acknowledgement log are retained for a minimum of 7 years to evidence that underwriters were informed before use, per file-documentation and market-conduct expectations.
Communication deadline met: notice issued at least 10 business days before the form effective date; the issued and effective dates on the log make the SLA auditable.

The form change and its rollout are governed by a change ticket in the ITSM platform cross-referenced to the SERFF tracking number and the PolicyCenter form-configuration change record.
The decision to deploy the form change and its communication plan is documented on the form record with the approver, approval date and the SERFF disposition it relies on.
Recipients documented by name/role on the distribution list (all underwriters and UW assistants in the affected LOB/state); the acknowledgement log records who received and confirmed the notice.
A quarterly sample of 20 approved form changes checked for timely, complete communication and recipient acknowledgement.

Missed or late communications are escalated to the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager; the form is held from binding in the affected LOB until notification and acknowledgement are complete.
The delegation/authority matrix (Authority Matrix v3.2) records who may approve a form change and its communication; sign-off traces to a role with the correct authority level.
In-scope effective dates = the DOI-approved effective date of each form change communicated this cycle; only changes with an effective date in the current window are in scope for this notification.
Applicable rule = the state form-filing approval that authorizes the form (SERFF tracking number and approval date) and the internal current-form-filings standard; both are cited on the notice.

Checked immediately before each form's scheduled effective/activation date; a form cannot be activated ahead of the confirmed approval or filing-effective date.

answers.value: The master register of filed policy forms, endorsements and rate filings with compliance status by state and line of business: every form/rate item the company relies on to write business, keyed to its SERFF tracking number.

Each register row shows: form/rate number and edition, state, LOB, SERFF tracking number, filing type, status (filed/approved/effective/withdrawn), effective date and PolicyCenter form id. Rows missing status, edition or effective date are flagged as incomplete.

Register row count reconciles to approved filings in SERFF and to active forms configured in PolicyCenter; three-way delta must be 0. Forms configured in PolicyCenter with no register/approval entry are logged as compliance gaps.
The register is versioned in SharePoint/SERFF with a change history and monthly snapshot memorialized in Archer GRC; each update carries editor, timestamp and version, retained 7 years.

The register structure and status taxonomy follow the filed-forms register standard (Register SOP v2); the SOP version governs field definitions and reconciliation rules.
Reconciliation is sensitive to timing: filings approved but not yet effective are tracked separately so pending-effective forms are not mistaken for active or missing entries.

Sampled register rows trace to the underlying SERFF filing packet and the PolicyCenter form configuration screen (tracking number, edition and effective date match all three).
Status values conform to the workflow (filed to approved to effective to withdrawn); no row sits in an invalid or skipped state, and withdrawn forms are deactivated in PolicyCenter.
Date fields (filed, approved, effective, withdrawn) are populated and ordered consistently; effective date is never earlier than approval date for prior-approval states.

answers.value: State DOI bulletins, regulatory notices and enacted legislative/regulatory changes across the states and lines of business the company writes, screened for anything requiring a new filing, form amendment or rate change.

Applicable rule = the statute/regulation or filing requirement the DOI objection cites (e.g. rating-factor support or form-language requirement) plus the state response-time rule; both are recorded on the objection record.

Submitted within the state's required prior-approval or file-and-use timeframe ahead of the intended effective date; the filing plan records target effective dates and the lead time each state requires.

Each filing shows: state, LOB, filing type (rate/form/rule), SERFF tracking number, required exhibits attached, filing fee, and intended effective date. A filing missing a mandatory exhibit or the actuarial memo is not submitted.

Filings submitted reconcile to the approved filing plan for the period; each planned state/LOB item is either submitted or has a documented deferral, delta 0. SERFF confirmation receipts are matched to each submission.
The submitted packet and SERFF confirmation are stored on the filing record and indexed in Archer GRC with tracking number, timestamp and version, retained 7 years.

The rate filing relies on an approved actuarial rate indication and methodology (Rate Review methodology, current version) supporting the requested rates; the version is cited in the actuarial memorandum.
The filing documents rate-level sensitivity (indicated vs selected change) and the impact on policyholders by band, as many states require a distributional/impact exhibit.
Rate changes above the state's flag threshold (e.g. +/-15% or a public-notice threshold) are treated as material and require enhanced actuarial justification and, in some states, prior approval.
The filing cites the state rate/form filing statute and the applicable filing type (prior-approval, file-and-use, use-and-file) governing the submission and its timeframe.
The complete filing packet and confirmations are retained a minimum of 7 years to support market-conduct and rate examinations.

Filings are submitted with sufficient lead time to obtain approval (prior-approval states) or satisfy the file-and-use notice period before the intended effective date; lead time and submission date are tracked per state.
A quarterly sample of 20 submitted filings inspected for completeness, correct filing type and timely submission.

PASS = filing submitted with all mandatory exhibits, correct filing type, and lead time meeting the state timeframe, with a SERFF confirmation. FAIL = missing exhibit, wrong filing type, or submission too late to meet the effective date.
Rejected/returned filings are corrected and resubmitted within 5 business days; a missed statutory timeframe is escalated to Regulatory Counsel and the target effective date is reset.
Field definitions (state, lob, filing_type, serff_tracking, exhibit_set, effective_date) come from the filing-plan data dictionary.
Control total = planned filings for the period equals submitted filings plus documented deferrals; each submission matched 1:1 to a SERFF confirmation receipt.

Approved methodology = the current actuarial rate-indication methodology and selected-rate rationale in the actuarial memorandum; parameters (loss trends, expense loads, target profit) sourced from the actuarial rate review supporting the filing.

Applicable rule = the state rate/form filing statute and its prescribed filing type/timeframe (prior-approval, file-and-use, use-and-file); the citation and SERFF tracking number are recorded on each filing.

answers.value: All open filings in regulatory review in SERFF: each pending rate/form/rule filing tracked from submission through objection, approval or disposition, by state and LOB, until it reaches a terminal status.
From SERFF submission date until approval/effective or withdrawal; status is refreshed at least weekly and immediately when a SERFF event (objection, approval) is received.

Each tracked filing shows: SERFF tracking number, state, LOB, current status, last-event date, next action, owner and target effective date. Filings without a current status or next action are flagged as stale.
Open filings in the tracker reconcile to open filings in SERFF; delta must be 0. Any SERFF filing not represented in the tracker (or vice versa) is corrected the same day.
The status tracker snapshots and SERFF event history are stored in Archer GRC/SharePoint with timestamp and version; retained 7 years alongside the filing record.

Filings stalled past expected review time or approaching an effective date without approval are logged as exceptions with disposition (follow up with DOI, extend effective date, or escalate) assigned to the filing owner.
The tracker records the filing type and governing state statute for each item so review-time expectations and any statutory deemer periods can be applied.
Status history and SERFF correspondence are retained a minimum of 7 years to document the regulatory review lifecycle for examination.
The tracker monitors each filing's target effective date and any statutory deemer/approval deadline, alerting when a filing risks missing its intended effective date.
A monthly sample of 25 in-review filings checked for accurate, current status versus SERFF.
PASS = tracker status matches SERFF for every sampled filing, with a defined next action and no stale (>2 weeks un-updated) records. FAIL = any status mismatch, missing next action, or stale record.

Mismatches are corrected the same day; filings at risk of missing an effective date are escalated to the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager and, if regulatory follow-up is needed, to Regulatory Counsel.
Acceptance = 100% of sampled filings show tracker status reconciled to SERFF with a current next action and no stale records.
Evidence (status snapshots, SERFF event exports, reconciliation notes) stored in Archer GRC under /filings/status-tracking/<period>/.

Applicable rule = the state filing statute governing each filing's review process, including any statutory deemer/approval period; the citation and SERFF tracking number are recorded on each tracked filing.
